head: claude/mi101-close-wedge-ledger
title: MI-101: make the close-wedge ledger's ABSENCE unreadable as a clean fleet
body:
## ⚠️ First: the incident question, answered — and a correction to the brief

**RULE ONE — I checked rather than relaying.** Both corrections below are in the direction that would have made this PR *understate* the problem.

### 1. NO INCIDENT. No `broker_cancel_wedged` close failure has occurred since MI-34 shipped.

**Window:** the MI-34 routing code began writing at **2026-09-02T08:33:53Z** — measured, not assumed, as the boundary where `close_failure` rows in `operator_alerts.jsonl` start carrying the `route` field (last row without: 08:17:06Z; merge commit `92215eca` was 08:30:33Z, so the deploy landed ~3m20s after).

**The instrument:** `runtime_logs/operator_alerts.jsonl` is purpose-built for exactly this question — `_append_operator_alert`'s docstring says the row must land *"or the downgrade itself becomes unmeasurable: 'we downgraded it' and 'it never fired' would render identically."* A ring row is written on **both** routes. It held **514 rows spanning 2026-09-01T09:25Z → 09-03T13:10Z**, un-trimmed (514 < the 600 trim threshold), so the window has no gap.

**The result — 101 `close_failure` rows since the deploy, ALL `route=page`:**

| route | share_hold | account | symbol | n |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `page` | `orders_still_resting` | alpaca_paper | GLD | 100 |
| `page` | `not_classified` | bybit_1 | AVAXUSDT | 1 |

**Zero `broker_cancel_wedged`. Zero `route=digest`.**

**The denominator, because "none found" needs one.** All 100 were on **`alpaca_paper`** — the exact venue whose classifier can emit the wedge value — so the classifying path ran 100 times on the right venue and returned a *different* value each time. It is not quiet because nothing was looked at.

**Positive controls, because a search returning nothing is not proof of absence:**

- My exact selector fires on a planted `broker_cancel_wedged` / `route=digest` row (0 hits live → 1 hit with one row planted).
- `classify_share_hold` on the **real GLD book today** returns `orders_still_resting`; the **same order** with `status=pending_cancel` returns `broker_cancel_wedged`, as does `pending_replace`. So the value is reachable, and the reason it is not appearing is that no Alpaca order is currently in `pending_cancel`.

**Corroborated on the two other channels named:** `/api/bot/logs?level=error` — 0 occurrences of any wedge token (expected, and it confirms the code's own documented claim that these alerts do not ride `outcomes.jsonl`); the live close-failure page text (`/api/bot/notifications`) — `alpaca_paper` GLD is **currently paging**, `share_hold: orders_still_resting`, consecutive failures 155. It is loudly in the **paging** channel, exactly as designed.

<details><summary>Incidental observation, NOT acted on — out of scope</summary>

`CLAUDE.md` records GLD OCO parent `2e843e04` as sitting at `pending_cancel` since 2026-08-27. Measured today via `/api/diag/alpaca_open_orders` it reads **`new`**, not `pending_cancel`, while the position is still open and the close is still failing (155 consecutive). So the wedge's *classification* has changed from what that row expects. That touches the classifier and the live wedge, both explicitly OUT of this work order's scope — flagged, not folded in.
</details>

### 2. The work order's defect (1) is NOT what the live digest is doing, and the truth is worse

The WO says the digest reports the ledger absent at a repo-relative path. **Not reproducible.** All **12** digest rows in `docs/claude/pending-pings.jsonl` say:

> `Standing close wedges: none (ledger read, 0 entries) — a real observation, not an absence of one.`

Every word of that was false. The chain:

```
trader never wrote the ledger
  -> diag answers present:false
  -> fetch_standing_wedges converts present:false into a SYNTHESISED empty ledger
  -> digest reports a clean fleet, and asserts it is a real observation
```

That inference was never available from a missing file — it is equally consistent with the writer never having run, which is what was true. **This is worse than the WO's "in neither channel" framing**, because `NOT EXAMINED` at least sends someone to look; a confident clean bill does not.

It is also this module's **own documented sin**: the `curl … || echo '{}'` idiom its docstring warns about, committed in Python inside the function written to prevent it — and shipped with a self-test (case 2) asserting the defect as correct behaviour.

**The path defect is real but LATENT, and is not the cause of the above.** `work_digest` read `REPO_ROOT/runtime_logs/`, which *agrees* with the fetch on a GitHub runner (no `DATA_DIR`) and diverges anywhere `DATA_DIR` is set — i.e. on the live VM, where the trader writes `/data/bot-data/runtime_logs/`. Fixed regardless; it is the `canonical-db-resolver` CWD-fallback class reappearing for a `runtime_logs` artifact.

### Why the file never existed

`sweep_vanished` returned **before touching disk** whenever no wedge was carried — the overwhelmingly common case — and `observe()` only writes when recording one. So a fleet that had never wedged wrote nothing, ever.

---

## The fix — all three parts on the same artifact, per the manager's ruling

**(a) PATH.** `work_digest` and `fetch_standing_wedges` both resolve through `runtime_logs_dir()`. The workflow drops its `--out` literal and its `mkdir -p`. **Verifiable as the WO asks — by the digest NAMING the path in its own output**, not by reading the code (self-test 22 asserts the resolved path is operator-visible).

**(b) PRESENT vs ABSENT.** The **WRITER** heartbeats an empty-but-present ledger from the sweep, floored at `CLOSE_WEDGE_HEARTBEAT_MINUTES` (default 15) so it costs one small atomic write per interval, **not one per monitor pass** — the original comment's concern is honoured, not dismissed. `last_sweep_at` is deliberately **not** advanced: liveness is not observation-continuity, and conflating them would let the first sweep after a wedge appears retire it as `vanished_unattributed`. `fetch_standing_wedges` no longer manufactures a ledger from `present: false` — only the writer can say "nothing is wedged".

**(c) FRESHNESS.** A present ledger is not a current one: a dead trader leaves a file that still parses and still reports zero wedges. The artifact **declares its own budget** (`heartbeat_interval_s`, `stale_after_intervals`) so reader and writer cannot drift, and the digest grades `fresh` / `stale` / `undeclared` / `unknown` — never collapsed. **The phrase "a real observation" is now reachable ONLY from a graded-fresh ledger.**

`_save` takes `now` so the stamp that gets graded is testable — a clock a test cannot set is a freshness rule nobody can write a failing test for.

## ⚠️ Deployment consequence, stated rather than glossed

**Until the trader restarts with the heartbeat, the digest will report `NOT EXAMINED` instead of today's false clean bill.** That is the honest state of a ledger nothing is writing, it is strictly more informative than what ships today, and it self-resolves on the next deploy. It is also a visible change to an operator channel, which is part of why this is held for approval.

## Test plan

- [x] `tests/test_close_wedge_downgrade.py` **28 → 34**. New: the sweep creates the ledger; it declares its own budget; the floor is honoured in **both** directions; the heartbeat never advances `last_sweep_at`; it never overwrites a store it could not parse; and a **positive control** that `vanished_unattributed` still fires, so the heartbeat has not broken the retirement path it now shares an entry point with.
- [x] `work_digest --self-test` **17 → 23**. Includes a **planted positive** where only the timestamp moves between `fresh` and `stale` — proving the grade reads the stamp and not something incidental — plus a regression control that the "real observation" phrase is unreachable from a stale or unknown ledger.
- [x] `fetch_standing_wedges --self-test` **9 → 10**, and **case 2 now asserts the OPPOSITE of what it asserted this morning**. Case 10 keeps three results apart: a failed fetch, an ABSENT ledger, and a writer-stamped empty one.
- [x] `pytest tests/test_close_wedge_downgrade.py tests/test_alpaca_wiring.py` — **92 passed**.
- [x] `ruff check .` clean **under the pinned `>=0.15,<0.16`** (a newer ruff floods the whole tree and is not what CI runs).
- [x] `scripts/ci/run_guards.py` — **PASS 66 · FAIL 0 · SKIP 19**, run on a **committed** tree so no guard was silently skipped. `layer-guard` needed `import-linter` installed locally; verified separately, 6 contracts kept, 0 broken.
- [x] `pr-landing-guard` → `state=declared_needs_approval`.
- [ ] CI green
- [ ] **The fleet observation, and it is NOT owed by this PR's green** — see below.

## ⚠️ What remains UNPROVEN

**The ledger has never been observed present on the fleet.** Everything above is a harness. The done-condition is:

1. After the trader restarts, `/api/diag/log_file?name=close_wedge_standing` reads `present: true` with a fresh `updated_at`.
2. A digest run **names `/data/bot-data/...` in its own output**.

A green CI is neither of those, and the backlog row is filed so this cannot be closed on the code alone.

## Scope

**IN:** the reader path, present-vs-absent, a freshness grade on the same artifact.

**OUT and untouched:** the close paths, `classify_share_hold`, and MI-34's routing decision. No order is placed, cancelled or modified; no config, risk cap, strategy, or deploy unit.

## Landing

`.github/pr-landing/mi101-close-wedge-ledger.json` — **tier 2, hold, `tier_2_3_needs_approval`**. Judged from the diff rather than copied: `src/runtime/close_wedge_standing.py` runs on the live trader's monitor sweep and this makes that sweep write where it previously returned early. Opened **ready, not draft** — the declaration holds it, not the draft flag.
